title: Reading a PCR as It Grows

scenes.tts: The first film grew DNA inside bacteria. Now two PCR tubes end equally bright. Did they start with the same amount? The answer hides in how the signal grew. Watch a bounded target become a curve that can be read.
scenes.caption: The first film grew DNA inside bacteria. Now two PCR tubes end equally bright. Did they start with the same amount? The answer hides in how the signal grew. Watch a bounded target become a curve that can be read.
scenes.visual: Reuse the first film's colour map: original DNA and outlines grey; primers yellow; new copies blue; supported results green; unresolved or failed results red. Two large tubes fill the frame with equally bright blue endpoints. Behind each, a hidden curve begins at a different height. Red question marks drift between the tubes.
scenes.narration: The first film grew DNA inside bacteria. Now two PCR tubes end equally bright. Did they start with the same amount? The answer hides in how the signal grew. Watch a bounded target become a curve that can be read.

scenes.visual: Transform the tubes into the title, 'Reading a PCR as It Grows'. A blue curve continues rising slowly behind the title.

scenes.tts: PCR starts with template DNA, primers, nucleotides, and heat-stable polymerase. A yellow primer binds each grey strand. Their three-prime ends point into the target. Polymerase extends from those ends. Primer placement sets the candidate boundaries for amplification.
scenes.caption: PCR starts with template DNA, primers, nucleotides, and heat-stable polymerase. A yellow primer binds each grey strand. Their 3' ends point into the target. Polymerase extends from those ends. Primer placement sets the candidate boundaries for amplification.
scenes.visual: A grey DNA duplex expands across most of the frame. Yellow primer arrows settle on opposite strands with large 3' labels pointing inward. A transparent yellow window appears between them. A blue polymerase block moves from each primer into that window while the flanking DNA stays grey.
scenes.narration: PCR starts with template DNA, primers, nucleotides, and heat-stable polymerase. A yellow primer binds each grey strand. Their 3' ends point into the target. Polymerase extends from those ends. Primer placement sets the candidate boundaries for amplification.

scenes.tts: Heating separates template strands. Cooling lets each primer pair with its site. Polymerase extends each primer, building blue DNA along grey template. Repeat the cycle, and earlier products become templates. Like a photocopier whose copies can be copied, the bounded target branches into a growing family.
scenes.caption: Heating separates template strands. Cooling lets each primer pair with its site. Polymerase extends each primer, building blue DNA along grey template. Repeat the cycle, and earlier products become templates. Like a photocopier whose copies can be copied, the bounded target branches into a growing family.
scenes.visual: Carry the same duplex through a circular three-step track labelled 'denature', 'anneal', and 'extend'. The strands separate, yellow primers dock, and blue bars grow. Each completed product moves back to the start and branches into more template rows. Keep fewer than six rows visible by grouping later copies.
scenes.narration: Heating separates template strands. Cooling lets each primer pair with its site. Polymerase extends each primer, building blue DNA along grey template. Repeat the cycle, and earlier products become templates. Like a photocopier whose copies can be copied, the bounded target branches into a growing family.

scenes.tts: During ideal early cycles, each completed target can seed another copy. Product can double every cycle, bending the graph upward. The blue curve is computed from starting amount times two raised to cycle number. Real reactions follow this only early.
scenes.caption: During ideal early cycles, each completed target can seed another copy. Product can double every cycle, bending the graph upward. The blue curve is computed from N = N₀ × 2ⁿ. Real reactions follow this only early.
scenes.visual: Compress the branching copies into a point on a large graph. Draw the early blue curve from computed values of N = N0 × 2^n, with the equation visible only on screen. A cycle marker moves right as copy groups accumulate. Label the blue segment 'ideal early model'.
scenes.narration: During ideal early cycles, each completed target can seed another copy. Product can double every cycle, bending the graph upward. The blue curve is computed from N = N₀ × 2ⁿ. Real reactions follow this only early.

scenes.tts: As product accumulates, amplification slows toward a plateau. Different starting amounts can finish at similar levels. Endpoint brightness loses how each reaction arrived there. Real-time PCR preserves that history by measuring fluorescence throughout the run, while early curves remain separated.
scenes.caption: As product accumulates, amplification slows toward a plateau. Different starting amounts can finish at similar levels. Endpoint brightness loses how each reaction arrived there. Real-time PCR preserves that history by measuring fluorescence throughout the run, while early curves remain separated.
scenes.visual: Add a second computed early blue curve from a lower N0. Extend both curves into dashed red bends that meet a common plateau. Mark only the dashed late portions 'schematic'. Two endpoint dots settle at nearly the same height, while the early solid blue portions remain separated.
scenes.narration: As product accumulates, amplification slows toward a plateau. Different starting amounts can finish at similar levels. Endpoint brightness loses how each reaction arrived there. Real-time PCR preserves that history by measuring fluorescence throughout the run, while early curves remain separated.

scenes.tts: A green threshold crosses both curves. One curve reaches it earlier, although both endpoints look alike. Which reaction began with more target? Think about how many rounds each needed to reach the same fluorescence.
scenes.caption: A green threshold crosses both curves. One curve reaches it earlier, although both endpoints look alike. Which reaction began with more target? Think about how many rounds each needed to reach the same fluorescence.
scenes.visual: A green horizontal threshold grows across the graph. Each curve gains a vertical guide at its crossing. Leave the guides unlabelled and do not highlight the answer. The two equal endpoint dots continue a slow pulse above the dashed schematic plateau.
scenes.narration: A green threshold crosses both curves. One curve reaches it earlier, although both endpoints look alike. Which reaction began with more target? Think about how many rounds each needed to reach the same fluorescence.

scenes.visual: Keep the threshold, crossing guides, and equal endpoints visible. A small cycle cursor moves once between the two crossings, then stops. Reveal no labels or answer.

scenes.tts: The earlier crossing came from more starting target. That reaction needed fewer rounds to reach the shared threshold. The crossing is the threshold cycle, written C T. With matched, near-perfect efficiency, an earlier threshold cycle means more starting template. The plateau cannot support that inference.
scenes.caption: The earlier crossing came from more starting target. That reaction needed fewer rounds to reach the shared threshold. The crossing is the threshold cycle, written Ct. With matched, near-perfect efficiency, an earlier Ct means more starting template. The plateau cannot support that inference.
scenes.visual: Turn the earlier guide green and label both crossings 'Ct' on screen. Animate the higher-start curve backward to a larger blue starting dot. Keep the later guide grey. Fade the endpoint dots toward grey while the crossing region enlarges to fill the frame.
scenes.narration: The earlier crossing came from more starting target. That reaction needed fewer rounds to reach the shared threshold. The crossing is the threshold cycle, written Ct. With matched, near-perfect efficiency, an earlier Ct means more starting template. The plateau cannot support that inference.

scenes.tts: Real-time quantitative PCR watches DNA accumulate. Reverse-transcription PCR starts differently. Reverse transcriptase copies RNA into complementary DNA, which PCR can amplify. Combining the steps measures an RNA target. The fluorescence still reports amplified DNA, not RNA directly.
scenes.caption: Real-time quantitative PCR watches DNA accumulate. Reverse-transcription PCR starts differently. Reverse transcriptase copies RNA into complementary DNA, or cDNA, which PCR can amplify. Combining the steps measures an RNA target. The fluorescence still reports amplified DNA, not RNA directly.
scenes.visual: Keep the graph at right. At left, a grey RNA ribbon passes through a grey-outlined 'reverse transcriptase' block and transforms into a blue cDNA bar. That bar flows into the same PCR cycle track and then into the plotted curve. Label the route 'RNA → cDNA → amplified DNA'.
scenes.narration: Real-time quantitative PCR watches DNA accumulate. Reverse-transcription PCR starts differently. Reverse transcriptase copies RNA into complementary DNA, or cDNA, which PCR can amplify. Combining the steps measures an RNA target. The fluorescence still reports amplified DNA, not RNA directly.

scenes.tts: A curve is evidence only within a controlled comparison. A tube with no template can expose contamination. For RNA, a tube without reverse transcriptase can expose genomic DNA. A known positive shows the assay works. Controls turn a glowing curve into an interpretable result.
scenes.caption: A curve is evidence only within a controlled comparison. A tube with no template can expose contamination. For RNA, a tube without reverse transcriptase can expose genomic DNA. A known positive shows the assay works. Controls turn a glowing curve into an interpretable result.
scenes.visual: The main graph shrinks slightly as three control tubes slide beside it. The 'no template' tube stays dark and gains a green outline. The 'no RT' tube, fed from the grey RNA ribbon with no reverse transcriptase block, stays dark and gains a green outline. The 'known positive' tube develops a blue curve and gains a green outline.
scenes.narration: A curve is evidence only within a controlled comparison. A tube with no template can expose contamination. For RNA, a tube without reverse transcriptase can expose genomic DNA. A known positive shows the assay works. Controls turn a glowing curve into an interpretable result.

scenes.tts: The early rising curve preserves information about starting amount. The endpoint mostly shows that product accumulated. Read the crossing under stated assumptions, then challenge the signal with controls. The useful measurement is when the curve arrives, not how bright it ends.
scenes.caption: The early rising curve preserves information about starting amount. The endpoint mostly shows that product accumulated. Read the crossing under stated assumptions, then challenge the signal with controls. The useful measurement is when the curve arrives, not how bright it ends.
scenes.visual: Re-expand the graph. A green spotlight follows the solid early curves and their threshold crossings. The dashed schematic plateau and endpoint dots recede into grey. The two control tubes remain at the edge, gently pulsing, while a green arrow connects starting dots to crossing points.
scenes.narration: The early rising curve preserves information about starting amount. The endpoint mostly shows that product accumulated. Read the crossing under stated assumptions, then challenge the signal with controls. The useful measurement is when the curve arrives, not how bright it ends.

scenes.visual: Clear everything to a dark field. Show one line only: 'Copy timing estimates input; endpoint abundance does not.'
